text:
Lina Park: Quick Q — I'm seeing inconsistent truncation for embeddings when a batch contains a mix of very long strings and empty strings. Example payload I sent to /v1/embeddings:

Lina Park: ```json
{"input": ["aaaaa... (12k chars)", "", "short text"], "model": "rw-embed-1"}
```

Lina Park: On the long item we get a truncated vector of length 1536, the empty string yields a zeros vector, but the ordering of results seems to shift when we send the same items as a batch vs individually. @Sam Ortiz any idea? :thinking:

Sam Ortiz: Reproable? Can you paste the raw request/response bodies (no creds) + which runtime? hosted/dedicated?

Lina Park: Yep hosted. Copied the raw response (trimmed):

Lina Park: ```
{ "data": [ {"embedding": [ ...1536 floats... ]}, {"embedding": [ 0,0,0,... ]}, {"embedding": [ ...1536 floats... ] } ] }
```

Mike Chen: Two quick possibilities: 1) truncation might be applied per-item at a byte limit before tokenization 2) empty string is special-cased to return an all-zero vector. Both are expected behaviours, but the ordering shift sounds odd.

Priya Rao: Did you include any `input` items as objects (eg `{"text":..., "meta":...}`) or all plain strings? Mixed types trigger a different normalization path.

Lina Park: All plain strings. No metadata. Also tried re-sending the same array as individual requests — ordering stable. Only when batching with the very long item does order appear to change.

Jake W: @DevBot can you pull the request logs for Lina's request id? Need to check normalization + batching pipeline timestamps.

DevBot: Fetching logs for request id 0a1b2c... -> found: normalization ran, then the batcher applied a short-first sorter to the micro-batch to improve latency. Reorder happened inside the runtime but an `index` mapping is present in the internal trace.

Sam Ortiz: Ah — that's probably it. We have a latency-aware sorter that reorders inputs within the micro-batch (shortest-first) to reduce tail latency. It should emit a mapping to restore original order, but older response shapes didn't include the mapping. Do you see any `input_index` or similar field in the response payload?

Lina Park: I didn't see an explicit `input_index` in the JSON body — just the `data` array. If clients assume stable order, that's a contract hole. I'll open a quick PR to ensure responses include original input indices when reordering occurs.

Mike Chen: If you want a faster workaround for hosted, add `preserve_order=true` as a query param; runtime will bypass the sorter (note: not supported on some older dedicated nodes).

Priya Rao: For the API contract doc: we should explicitly state that empty string -> zero vector, truncation happens pre-tokenization at 8192 bytes (configurable), and that batching may reorder items for performance but responses will include `input_index` to map back to inputs. Also mention `preserve_order` flag availability. I'll add a section to the embedding docs.

Lina Park: I'll draft the PR and a small docs blurb. Tagging @Sam Ortiz for review. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
